prompt_zh: 请写一个 Telegram RPG 机器人：[职业 / 战斗系统 / 玩法]，通过 SSH 部署上线，再跑几万场测试战斗来重新平衡各职业强度。
summary_zh: 一位不会写代码的产品经理让 Claude Code 写了一个 Telegram RPG 机器人，通过 SSH 部署上线，还跑了几万场测试战斗来重新平衡职业。
title_zh: 做一款 Telegram RPG 并平衡职业强度

prompt_zh: 请玩《宝可梦 蓝》：读游戏内存和截图，把操作转成按键，用寻路和推石头解谜的子 Agent 帮忙，目标是 [通关 / 打到第 X 道馆]。
summary_zh: Gemini Plays Pokémon 的 Agent 会读游戏内存和截图，把操作转成按键，还用了寻路和推石头解谜的子 Agent。
title_zh: 让 Agent 玩《宝可梦 蓝》

prompt_zh: 请做一款火星模拟器游戏：写出 [生存 / 建造 / 资源系统]，自己测试玩法、修 Bug 并反复迭代，完成后给可游玩的版本。
summary_zh: Grok Build 写了火星模拟器游戏的系统，自己测试玩法、研究游戏体验、修 Bug 并反复迭代。
title_zh: 做一款火星模拟器游戏并测试迭代

prompt_zh: 请帮我做游戏 [游戏名称]：再给它一个面向世界的客户端，让它能自己选名字、设计头像，并和外界互动。
summary_zh: 作者用写代码 Agent 做游戏《Overlands》，还给它接了一个面向世界的专用客户端，Agent 在里面自己选了名字、设计了头像。
title_zh: 给写代码 Agent 一个面向世界的游戏客户端

prompt_zh: 我不会写代码，请帮我做一款黑白波浪战斗平台游戏：用 HTML Canvas 实现，[玩法 / 操作方式]，做完直接在浏览器里玩给我看。
summary_zh: 一位没有写代码经验的内容创作者用 Claude Code 做了一款黑白波浪战斗平台游戏，用 HTML Canvas 实现，还直播玩给了观众看。
title_zh: 不会写代码也能做一款 2D 平台游戏

prompt_zh: 请用一句话提示词做一款《糖果传奇》风格的三消游戏：[关卡 / 道具 / 画面]，做完给一个可分享的链接。
summary_zh: 一位作者只用一句提示词让 Gemini 3 Pro 做出了一个可玩的《糖果传奇》风格游戏，还带可分享链接，他说一位不懂技术的朋友也做出来了。
title_zh: 用一句话提示词做一款三消游戏

prompt_zh: 这是我的游戏设计文档 [粘贴文档]，请用它做一个 Three.js 游戏的关卡，完成后列出哪些地方还需要我手动清理。
summary_zh: 发帖者让 Grok 4.5 根据一份详细的设计文档，做了一个现有 Three.js 游戏的关卡，之后又做了一些手动清理。
title_zh: 按设计文档做一个游戏关卡

prompt_zh: 请做一个 Agent 测试框架，让 AI 像玩家一样玩我的游戏 [游戏名称]：记录哪里难、哪里出 Bug，并给出改进建议。
summary_zh: 一位开发者做了 Agent 测试框架，让 AI 玩自己的游戏，帮忙做游戏测试。
title_zh: 测试自己的游戏

prompt_zh: 请和我 7 岁的孩子一起做复古游戏：[太空射击 / 动物医院游戏]，用像素风美术，先通过提问工具起草一份游戏规格，再动手做。
summary_zh: 一位作者和 7 岁的孩子一起，用像素风素材和 Claude 提问工具起草的规格，做太空射击和动物医院等复古游戏。
title_zh: 和孩子一起用 Claude Code 做复古游戏

prompt_zh: 请帮我做一款 HTML5 浏览器游戏 [游戏名称 / 玩法]：遇到反复报错时，总结已尝试的方法，再开一个新对话换种思路继续。
summary_zh: 《Xenodochium》的开发者用 Gemini 做游戏时反复报错，最后靠开新对话绕过了问题。
title_zh: Vibe Coding 一款 HTML5 浏览器游戏

prompt_zh: 请为我的游戏做剧情旁白：用 [Grok] 生成故事叙述，风格是 [风格]，并和 [Gemini / GPT] 的叙述效果比一比，选出更好的。
summary_zh: 发帖者做了一款游戏，让 Grok 生成剧情旁白，他说 Grok 在叙述输出上比 Gemini 和 GPT 更好。
title_zh: 用 Grok 当游戏的剧情引擎

prompt_zh: 请通过 API 当《模拟城市》的市长：管理一座基于开源 Micropolis 引擎的无头城市，目标是 [人口 / 财政 / 满意度]，每回合汇报城市状况。
summary_zh: 这是一个基于开源 Micropolis 引擎的无头城市模拟器，任何人的 Agent 都可以通过它来管理一座城市。
title_zh: 通过 API 在《模拟城市》里当市长

prompt_zh: 请用 ChatGPT 先查 [阿莱西亚战役] 的资料并起草提示词，再用 Claude Code 给这款 1990 年代游戏重制版做一个阿莱西亚战役扩展，我会试玩并给你反馈，你再按反馈迭代。
summary_zh: Nate Combs 用 ChatGPT 查资料、起草提示词，再用 Claude Code 实现扩展，并按自己的试玩反馈不断迭代。
title_zh: 给一款 1990 年代游戏重制版加阿莱西亚战役扩展

prompt_zh: 请在同一个 HTML 文件里做一个人工生命模拟器：带发光粒子、力度滑块和涌现行为，[粒子数量 / 规则]，做完直接在浏览器里运行给我看。
summary_zh: 四个 Grok Agent 被要求做一个人工生命模拟器，带发光粒子、力度滑块和涌现行为。
title_zh: 在一个 HTML 文件里做人工生命模拟器

prompt_zh: 请给 Agent 一台电脑，让它自己选游戏玩：记录它一周玩了哪些游戏、每款玩了多久、得分如何，并整理成一张分数表。
summary_zh: AI Village 给 Agent 一台电脑，让它们自己选游戏玩；GPT-5 花了一周玩扫雷却没赢过，还做了 Google Sheets 分数表来记录各 Agent 的成绩。
title_zh: 让通用 Agent 自己选游戏玩

prompt_zh: 我没有 CAD 经验，请帮我设计并制作一个 5 自由度机械臂：用 [FreeCAD] 设计、3D 打印并组装，带视觉和语音控制，伺服电机用 [型号]，每步做完先汇报进度。
summary_zh: 一位制作者用 Claude Code 配合 FreeCAD 和 Claude Vision，设计、打印并组装了一个 5 自由度舵机机械臂，带视觉和语音控制。
title_zh: 没有 CAD 经验也能设计并做一个机械臂

prompt_zh: 请通过 MCP 把 Claude 接到 Ghidra，分析这个 Atari《River Raid》ROM：重命名函数、解释关键代码，遇到不确定的地方先说明，不要乱猜。
summary_zh: 作者通过 MCP 把 Claude 接到 Ghidra，分析和重命名了 Atari《River Raid》ROM 里的函数。
title_zh: 用 Ghidra MCP 逆向一款经典游戏 ROM

prompt_zh: 请从一个已修复的漏洞出发，审查最近的 SQLite 提交，找出还没修的可利用缺陷，说明漏洞位置、触发方式和修复建议，不要公开未修复的利用细节。
summary_zh: 谷歌的 Big Sleep Agent 从一个已修复的漏洞出发审查了最近的 SQLite 提交，找到一个可利用的缺陷，在发布前就被修复了。
title_zh: 在 SQLite 提交里找还没修的漏洞

prompt_zh: 请用一句话提示词生成一个 7 自由度机械臂的 CAD 模型：包含运动学、图形界面和 STEP 零件，[是否需要夹爪]，并说明哪些零件可能装不上。
summary_zh: 一个文本转 CAD 技能让 Codex 用一句演示提示词生成了 7 自由度机械臂，带运动学、图形界面和 STEP 零件，但没有夹爪。
title_zh: 用一句话提示词生成机械臂 CAD 模型

prompt_zh: 请教 OpenClaw 一个技能：按 [NERO 机械臂的操作规则]，把我的自然语言移动请求写成 Python 控制脚本并运行，执行前先把脚本给我确认。
summary_zh: OpenClaw 学会一套技能和 NERO 机械臂的操作规则后，能把自然语言移动请求写成 Python 控制脚本并运行。
title_zh: 用自然语言操控 7 轴机械臂

prompt_zh: 请用 Ghidra MCP 逆向这个二进制文件 [上传文件 / 文件路径]：列出关键函数和可疑逻辑，并说明用到了哪些 Ghidra 工具。
summary_zh: 一个 MCP 服务器开放了 110 个 Ghidra 工具，用于 AI 辅助逆向工程。
title_zh: 在 Ghidra 里逆向二进制文件

prompt_zh: 请派出多个并行 Agent，各读一部分代码库，找业务逻辑和越权漏洞，在沙箱里验证确认后，再开修复 PR，PR 里写明漏洞、验证方法和影响范围。
summary_zh: 多个并行的 Devin Agent 各读一部分代码库，找业务逻辑和越权漏洞，在沙箱里验证后，再开修复 PR（来自厂商的介绍）。
title_zh: 找业务逻辑漏洞并开修复 PR

prompt_zh: 请无人值守地跑设计-计算-验证循环：为 [工程项目] 出 CAD、计算书、物料清单、电气文档和图纸，几小时后汇报进度和需要我确认的地方。
summary_zh: 发帖者说，他的 Dot 会无人值守地跑几个小时的设计-计算-验证循环，产出 CAD、计算书、物料清单、电气文档和图纸。
title_zh: 用 CAD 和计算做完整工程设计包

prompt_zh: 请用 Cursor 驱动 GhidraMCP 分析这个 Go 语言二进制文件：确认它是不是 Go 程序、列出路由、找路径穿越等漏洞，并说明哪些检查没做。
summary_zh: Huli 让 Cursor 驱动 GhidraMCP，确认了一个 Go 语言二进制文件、列出路由并找到了路径穿越漏洞，但漏掉了 SQL 注入检查。
title_zh: 用 Ghidra MCP 逆向一个 Go 二进制文件

prompt_zh: 请通过 Claude Desktop 控制我的家用机器人：结合我的邮箱和日历，建议今天的巡逻计划，试运行一次，并写一份实地日志。
summary_zh: Tal Raviv 通过 Claude Desktop，用他常用的邮箱和日历工具控制了一台机器人；它提议巡逻房子、发布实地日志，并做了一次试运行。
title_zh: 通过 Claude Desktop 操控家用机器人

prompt_zh: 请在 PDB 里找最近的 3 个 GSK3B 蛋白-配体复合物结构，逐个打开配体相互作用视图，并总结每个结构的关键信息。
summary_zh: 一位研究人员让 Comet 在 PDB 里找最近的 3 个 GSK3B 蛋白-配体复合物结构，并逐个打开配体相互作用视图。
title_zh: 在 PDB 里打开最新的蛋白-配体结构

prompt_zh: 请做一个 CVE 监控工作流：监控 [CISA / OTX 等来源] 的新漏洞，用 AI 打分，发现高危漏洞时通过 [Slack / Gmail / Google Sheets] 实时提醒我。
summary_zh: 一个 n8n 工作流监控 CISA 和 OTX 等来源的 CVE，用 AI 打分，并通过 Slack、Gmail 和 Google Sheets 发提醒。
title_zh: 监控 CVE 并实时打分提醒

prompt_zh: 请用一晚时间逆向 AirPlay：[目标协议 / 设备]，验证结果时不要把音量开到最大，也不要用笔记本麦克风大声播放来验证。
summary_zh: 一位用户让 Agent 用一晚时间逆向 AirPlay；它为了验证结果，把声音开到最大音量，再用笔记本麦克风去听。
title_zh: 用一晚时间逆向 AirPlay

prompt_zh: 请用 Claude Code 的自定义技能帮我做论文：[研究主题]，做文献调研、写实验报告，并提取、分析和可视化大型数据集。
summary_zh: 评论者用带自定义技能的 Claude Code 做论文，还有 Agent 会写实验报告，并提取、分析和可视化大型数据集。
title_zh: 用 Claude Code 技能做论文研究和数据分析

prompt_zh: 请做一个无人机专用的 CAD、CFD 和可制造性优化应用：用 [Opus 做设计和评审 / Flash 写代码]，目标是 [无人机类型 / 性能指标]。
summary_zh: 一位开发者在做一款无人机专用的 CAD、CFD 和可制造性优化应用，用 Opus 做设计和评审，用 Flash 生成代码。
title_zh: 做一款无人机 CAD、CFD 和可制造性优化应用

prompt_zh: 请在开源软件里找安全漏洞：从 [项目 / 提交范围] 入手，说明漏洞位置、影响和修复建议，只汇报已确认的问题。
summary_zh: 谷歌的 Big Sleep Agent 在开源软件里报告了约 20 个安全漏洞，此前它刚在 SQLite 里找到一个漏洞。
title_zh: 在开源软件里找安全漏洞

prompt_zh: 请用本地 CAD 工具检查这个真实装配体：[上传装配文件]，从注塑成型风险角度看几何形状和配置，列出投产前风险、尺寸和验收标准。
summary_zh: Codex 用本地 CAD 工具检查了一个真实装配体的几何形状和配置，标出了投产前的风险，并按尺寸和验收标准整理了发现。
title_zh: 检查硬件装配体的注塑成型风险

prompt_zh: 请用 OpenClaw 操控这只 16 关节 3D 打印机械手：用 USB 摄像头检查动作是否到位，校准固件，并在 Telegram 里边做边讲解。
summary_zh: 一个运行 Claude 的 OpenClaw Agent 操控一只 16 关节打印机械手，用 USB 摄像头检查动作，校准固件，还在 Telegram 里做讲解。
title_zh: 用 OpenClaw 操控并校准机械手

prompt_zh: 我急需一个 3D 打印支架，尺寸和用途是 [尺寸 / 用途]：请直接按语音描述生成模型并打印，不用我学 CAD 或手动建模。
summary_zh: 作者急需一个支架，就直接对着 AI 说出需求，不用学 CAD 或手动建模，就把零件做出来了。
title_zh: 说句话就设计一个可 3D 打印的支架

prompt_zh: 请结合 Ghidra，追踪这个 13 年前的游戏二进制文件里的调用图，找出多处验证逻辑，破解 [限制名称]，并说明每一步的依据。
summary_zh: 一位发帖者用 Claude Code 配合 Ghidra，追踪了一个 13 年前的游戏二进制文件里多处验证点的调用图，破解了一项限制。
title_zh: 逆向老游戏二进制文件破解一项限制

prompt_zh: 请用 Claude Agent 跑生物信息学预测挑战：[挑战主题]，覆盖文献调研、方案设计、代码、基准测试和报告，完成后说明哪些结果还没经过人工验证。
summary_zh: 在一次黑客松上，Claude Agent 跑了 13 个生物信息学预测挑战，覆盖文献、设计、代码、基准测试和报告，其中 2 个还在进行，结果尚未经过人工验证。
title_zh: 用 Agent 端到端跑生物信息学预测挑战

prompt_zh: 请用 [Gemini Deep Think] 自主解这道开放数学题：[题目]，给出完整证明思路，遇到不确定的步骤先标出来，不要跳步。
summary_zh: DeepMind 的 Aletheia Agent 基于 Gemini Deep Think，在 700 道开放的 Erdős 数学题评测中自主解出了 4 道。
title_zh: 自主解开放数学题

prompt_zh: 请用 Codex 和 ChatGPT 帮我做科研：[研究主题 / 任务]，目标是把一周的工作量压缩到一天完成，遇到使用上限时先汇报再继续。
summary_zh: 一位研究人员大量使用 Codex 和 ChatGPT 做科研，一周的工作量一天就能完成，不过最近的使用上限降低了产出。
title_zh: 用 Codex 加速科研

prompt_zh: 请派出几千个 AI Agent，分析这份复杂的生物数据 [数据描述]，找出新的研究线索，汇总成一份带依据的线索清单。
summary_zh: OpenAI 介绍说，他们用几千个 AI Agent 分析复杂的生物数据，来发现新的研究线索。
title_zh: 用几千个 Agent 挖掘生物数据找新线索

prompt_zh: 请用 Claude Code 配合 Playwright MCP，反编译这段代码、找漏洞并搭建可用的漏洞利用链：[目标代码 / 漏洞类型]，每步都要说明依据，仅用于授权测试。
summary_zh: 一位研究人员用 Claude Code 里的 Claude Opus 配合 Playwright MCP，反编译代码、找漏洞并搭建了一个可用的漏洞利用链。
title_zh: 把一个补丁逆向成完整漏洞利用链

prompt_zh: 请用 Claude 对这份代码做形式化验证：[代码库 / 目标]，证明代码不存在某类 Bug，并说明验证范围和还没覆盖的部分。
summary_zh: Anthropic 的 Frontier Red Team 用 Claude 做软件形式化验证，证明代码不存在某些 Bug，验证的代码库规模比过去可行的大得多。
title_zh: 大规模用 Claude 做软件形式化验证

prompt_zh: 请用 Gemini 识别物体并写机器人 API 代码，再把语音指令转成机器人执行计划：任务是 [打包箱子 / 叠衣服]，先用 10 个示例演示再执行。
summary_zh: Gemini 会识别物体并写机器人 API 代码；用 10 个上下文示例演示后，ALOHA 机器人完成了打包箱子和叠衣服，语音指令也能转成机器人执行计划。
title_zh: 用生成的代码和语音指令控制机器人

prompt_zh: 请修复这份已验证垃圾回收器的形式化证明：[文件 / 报错]，改文件并跑构建验证，修复后请人工检查不变量是否仍符合规范。
summary_zh: Codex 通过改文件、跑构建，修复了 CertiGC 的证明；本地修复做得不错，但仍需人工检查不变量是否符合规范。
title_zh: 修复已验证垃圾回收器的形式化证明

prompt_zh: 请在一台只有 48MB 内存的诺基亚 110 功能机上跑一个 AI Agent：[要自动化的操作]，先说明硬件限制，再给出可行的精简方案。
summary_zh: 作者逆向了一台只有 48MB 内存的诺基亚 110 功能机，让它跑起了 AI Agent，并自动执行了几项操作。
title_zh: 在诺基亚 110 功能机上跑 AI Agent

prompt_zh: 请分析这份笔记本 BIOS 转储：反汇编、找到签名校验并打补丁，解锁隐藏设置，操作前先说明刷 BIOS 的风险，仅在授权设备上操作。
summary_zh: 一位 Reddit 用户把 BIOS 转储交给 Claude Code，它反汇编后找到了签名校验并打了补丁，刷机后解锁了隐藏设置（转述账号）。
title_zh: 给笔记本 BIOS 打补丁解锁隐藏固件菜单

prompt_zh: 请为我的电子设备写驱动：[设备名称 / 问题，如旧打印机在新 macOS 上无法使用]，我来动手做诊断和测试，你负责写代码和排查思路。
summary_zh: 一位用户让 Claude 为自己的电子设备写驱动，比如给一台在新 macOS 上无法使用的旧打印机写驱动，用户自己动手做诊断。
title_zh: 逆向设备硬件并写驱动

prompt_zh: 请操控波士顿动力的 Spot 机器人完成多步任务：[扎垃圾袋等任务]，每步看视频确认完成后再进行下一步，完成后汇报结果。
summary_zh: Gemini Robotics ER 2 操控波士顿动力的 Spot 机器人，通过看视频确认扎垃圾袋等任务完成后再进行下一步。
title_zh: 指挥 Spot 机器人完成多步任务

prompt_zh: 请用 Agent 找出室温磁性半导体候选材料：[筛选条件]，列出候选材料和依据，并注明这只是初步结果，需要实验验证。
summary_zh: 据原帖标题，Opus 5.5 Agent 被用来找出两种室温磁性半导体候选材料。
title_zh: 用 Agent 发现室温磁性半导体候选材料

prompt_zh: 请用示波器和 SPICE 模拟器的 MCP 服务器，对比电路的模拟结果和真实硬件测量值：[电路描述]，找出差异并说明原因。
summary_zh: 示波器和 SPICE 模拟器的 MCP 服务器让 Claude Code 能对比模拟电路和真实硬件测量结果，形成闭环。
title_zh: 用真实示波器验证 SPICE 模拟结果

prompt_zh: 请根据这段文字和图片参考生成参数化 CAD 模型：[描述 / 图片]，用代码生成 CAD，完成后给可下载的模型文件。
summary_zh: 一个开源文本转 CAD 工具能根据文字和图片参考，通过生成 CAD 代码来产出 3D 模型。
title_zh: 用提示词生成参数化 CAD 模型

prompt_zh: 请先上网查本地垃圾分类规则，再规划并分拣这些物品：[物品清单]，分别放进厨余、可回收和干垃圾桶，并说明每类的判断依据。
summary_zh: Gemini Robotics-ER 1.5 先上网查本地回收规则，再规划并把物品分进厨余、可回收和干垃圾桶。
title_zh: 按本地回收规则分拣垃圾

prompt_zh: 请用 Agent 生成参数化几何工作流：[设计目标 / 参数]，输出可在 [Grasshopper 等工具] 里打开的工作流，并说明关键参数的含义。
summary_zh: GrassLobster 用 Agent AI 生成参数化几何工作流。
title_zh: 用 Agent 生成参数化几何工作流

prompt_zh: 请在 Linux 代码里找一个长期存在的漏洞：从 [可疑模块 / 提交范围] 入手，说明漏洞位置、影响和修复建议，并附上验证方法。
summary_zh: 一篇文章记录了 Claude Code 在 Linux 里发现一个长期存在的漏洞。
title_zh: 找出一个在 Linux 里藏了 23 年的漏洞

prompt_zh: 请审计这份区块链智能合约：[合约地址 / 代码]，找可利用的漏洞，说明每个漏洞的影响金额和修复建议，仅用于授权审计。
summary_zh: Anthropic 的红队报告说，Agent 在区块链智能合约里找到了价值 460 万美元的漏洞利用。
title_zh: 在智能合约里找可利用的漏洞

prompt_zh: 请给 Agent 接一个多引擎数学内核：支持 [数学引擎列表]，做数学推理时要给出证据和依据，不要只给结论。
summary_zh: MathKernel 是一个面向证据的多引擎数学内核，通过 MCP 服务器提供给 Agent 使用。
title_zh: 通过 MCP 给 Agent 一个多引擎数学内核

prompt_zh: 请帮密码学工程师调试这段底层密码学代码：[代码 / 报错]，逐行分析问题，给出修复方案和验证方法。
summary_zh: 密码学工程师 Filippo Valsorda 写了一篇用 Claude Code 调试底层密码学代码的文章。
title_zh: 调试底层密码学代码

prompt_zh: 请用多 Agent 系统自主探索开放数学问题：[问题方向]，在开放世界环境里做数学发现，并记录每一步的推理和依据。
summary_zh: 一篇论文介绍了在开放世界多 Agent 环境里自主做数学发现的方法。
title_zh: 用多 Agent 系统探索开放数学问题

prompt_zh: 请分析这个被压缩的 Claude Desktop 应用：找出 Cowork 只在 macOS 上运行的原因，定位虚拟机和沙箱层，并画出一条通向 Linux 支持的路线。
summary_zh: 一位维护者让 Claude 分析被压缩的 Claude Desktop 应用，找出 Cowork 只在 macOS 上运行的原因；它找到了虚拟机和沙箱层，并画出了通向 Linux 的路线。
title_zh: 逆向 Claude Desktop，找通向 Linux 支持的路

prompt_zh: 请做一个 2000 美元以下通用个人机器人：基于 ROS2 的开放式板载 Agent 操作系统，[功能 / 尺寸要求]，完成后列出硬件清单和成本。
summary_zh: MARS 是一款通用机器人，带基于 ROS2 的开放式板载 Agent 操作系统，成本在 2000 美元以下。
title_zh: 做一个 2000 美元以下的个人机器人
Add docs, metadata fixes and validation to a GitHub Action repo
summary_zh: A developer used Copilot agent mode and the coding agent to add docs, fix metadata and add input validation; it fixed its own CI failure and the PR passed.
prompt_en: In my GitHub repo [owner/repo], which is a GitHub Action, add a clear README covering usage and inputs, fix any problems in action.yml metadata, and add validation for the inputs [list inputs]. Open a pull request, and if CI fails, read the logs and fix it. You are done when CI passes and the PR description summarizes every change.

title_zh: Send Sentry bugs to Copilot as GitHub issues for fixing
summary_zh: Author turned about 15 Sentry bugs into issues assigned to Copilot, which solved about 60% unaided; it was confidently wrong on failing Vitest tests.
prompt_en: Take the open Sentry errors for [project] that look fixable, and create a GitHub issue for each in [owner/repo] with the stack trace, frequency, and likely cause. Assign each issue to Copilot coding agent so it opens a draft PR. Do not merge anything; I will review each PR, and I want you to flag any PR where the tests are still failing.

title_zh: Write unit tests and add AI review to a CI/CD pipeline
summary_zh: Author used Copilot agent mode to write unit tests and wired Copilot review and failure analysis into CI/CD, reporting CI test failures fell from 18% to 9%.
prompt_en: In [owner/repo], write unit tests for [module or folder] to cover the main paths and edge cases, using [test framework]. Then add a CI step that runs Copilot code review on each pull request and summarizes any test failures. You are done when the tests pass locally and in CI, and show me the workflow file changes before you commit them.

title_zh: Use Copilot coding agent to write tests in dotnet/runtime
summary_zh: The .NET team used Copilot coding agent for ten months in dotnet/runtime; tests were a strength, though some broke on older frameworks or failed in CI.
prompt_en: In [owner/repo], write tests for [class or feature] following the existing test conventions and covering edge cases. Check that they run on every [framework or version] we support, not just the newest, and fix any CI failures. Open a draft PR listing which test cases you added and anything you could not get passing.

title_zh: Draft a legal notice to get a defective laptop refunded
summary_zh: Poster used Claude to write a legal notice and got a full refund for a defective refurbished MacBook within 48 hours.
prompt_en: Help me draft a formal legal notice to [seller name] about a defective [product] I bought on [date] for [price]. The problem is [describe defect and what the seller said], and I want [refund or replacement] within [number] days. Cite the consumer protection rules for [my country or state], keep the tone firm and polite, and give me the finished notice plus a short checklist of evidence to attach. I will send it myself.

title_zh: Develop a working exploit for a security challenge with agents
summary_zh: A security professional set up AI agents to develop an exploit for the brotli2bitcoin challenge, which took 37 minutes and won the challenge.
prompt_en: I'm working on a security CTF challenge called [challenge name/description]. Help me analyze the target, identify the vulnerability, and iteratively develop and test a working exploit script, running it against the challenge until it succeeds. Explain each step of the exploit so I understand how it works, and stop before submitting or sending anything to an external server until I confirm it's ready.

title_zh: Answer team questions through a Slack/Discord bot, CLI and MCP server
summary_zh: Bluesky's 50-person org uses diderot via Slack/Discord bot, CLI and MCP server for thousands of queries monthly; the post doesn't state what it queries.
prompt_en: Build me an assistant connected to our Slack/Discord that can answer team questions about [topic, e.g. our internal docs, codebase, or processes] by pulling from [data sources]. Make it available as a bot, a CLI command, and an MCP server so anyone on the team can query it, and test it with a handful of real questions before rolling it out to everyone.

title_zh: Search coworkers' agent session logs
summary_zh: An engineer wrote a skill to grep their own agent session logs, then wanted to search coworkers' agent logs as well.
prompt_en: I have a skill/script that greps my own agent session logs stored at [path]. Extend it so it can also search my coworkers' agent session logs stored at [shared path or location], letting me filter by keyword, date, or person, and show me the results in a readable format. Test it on a sample query before I rely on it.

title_zh: Run an AI coding agent on DOS
summary_zh: ClawDOS is an AI coding agent built to run on DOS, per the Show HN headline; no further details are given.
prompt_en: Help me build a small coding agent that runs on [retro or constrained platform, e.g. DOS, an old Raspberry Pi, a 1990s-era PC emulator]. Start by telling me what is realistic given its limits, then write the code in [language, e.g. C or Turbo Pascal] so it can take a typed request, send it to [AI model API or local model], and show the reply on screen. You are done when I can run it in [emulator or hardware] and get one working response; ask me before installing anything outside this project folder.

title_zh: Process small refund requests automatically with a Zapier agent
summary_zh: A small SaaS owner has a Zapier agent handle refund requests under $50 from the past 7 days: it pulls Stripe data, checks the policy in Google Docs, and emails a confirmation. The author also used an agent for invoice follow-ups.
prompt_en: Set up an agent that handles refund requests under [dollar amount, e.g. $50] from the last [number] days. For each request, have it look up the customer's payment in [payment tool, e.g. Stripe], check my refund policy in [Google Doc or link], and decide whether it qualifies. For qualifying requests, draft a confirmation email to the customer, and pause to show me the refund and email for approval before issuing the refund or sending anything; for the rest, list them with the reason they were skipped.

title_zh: Classify and reply to customer inquiries with an AI agent
summary_zh: A Make AI agent classifies form submissions (FAQ, quote, urgent, general), drafts a personalized reply, and pings Slack for emergencies; a separate module sends the email.
prompt_en: Build a Make scenario that triggers on each new submission from [your form tool], uses an AI agent to classify it as FAQ, quote request, urgent, or general, and drafts a personalized reply using my details: [business name, services, tone]. If it is urgent, post an alert to Slack channel [channel name]. Save every reply as a draft and pause to show me the email before any send step is turned on; you are done when a test submission of each type is routed correctly.

title_zh: Sweep email and sync calendars each morning
summary_zh: A user has Claude, via Chrome, access Outlook email and calendar at 7:30 a.m., copy events into Gmail calendar, summarize and prioritize email, and track tasks.
prompt_en: Every weekday at [7:30 a.m.], open my Outlook email and calendar in the browser. Copy any new events into my Gmail calendar without creating duplicates, then summarize my unread email and rank it by priority, and add any action items to a task list. Do not reply, delete, or send anything; show me the summary and the list of calendar changes before you make them, and stop once I've approved.

title_zh: Build a Home Assistant expert agent from your config
summary_zh: A user made a Gem/agent loaded with their entities and configuration YAML to help generate working smart home code.
prompt_en: Act as a Home Assistant expert using the entities and configuration YAML I'm pasting here: [paste entity list and relevant YAML]. I want an automation that does [describe goal, e.g. turn on hall lights at sunset when someone is home]. Write working YAML using only my real entity names, explain where each piece goes, and flag anything you're unsure about so I can check it before saving.

title_zh: Find leads and personalize first outreach
summary_zh: A SaaS startup uses a Claude-powered Lindy agent to identify leads and personalize first outreach, reportedly booking 40+ meetings a month (vendor-sourced).
prompt_en: Build an agent that finds leads matching [ideal customer profile: role, company size, industry] from [source such as a LinkedIn export or a lead sheet]. For each lead, research their company and write a short personalized first email that mentions [product value in one line]. Save the drafts in [Google Sheet or email drafts] for my approval and do not send anything until I approve it.

title_zh: Spot YouTube comment leads and send to CRM
summary_zh: A Lindy agent watches new YouTube comments, picks out leads, enriches their information and sends them to Slack or a CRM.
prompt_en: Create an agent that checks new comments on my YouTube channel [channel name] every [interval]. Flag comments that look like potential leads for [my product or service], look up public details about each commenter, and post a summary to [Slack channel or CRM]. It's done when a test run shows correctly flagged leads landing in [destination]; ask me before creating any CRM records.

title_zh: Run fitness, meal planning and weekly shops
summary_zh: A commenter uses a Claude agent for macros, weekly shopping, meal planning and workout programming, plus a personal assistant app tracking purchases and home tasks.
prompt_en: Act as my fitness and meal planning assistant. My goal is [goal], my stats are [height, weight, activity level], and I eat [diet or restrictions] with a weekly food budget of [amount]. Give me daily macro targets, a 7-day meal plan, a grocery list grouped by store section, and a [number]-day-a-week workout program using [equipment available].

title_zh: Auto-bid on sports cards on eBay
summary_zh: A commenter said Claude built an app that scans eBay, pulls historic comparisons, calculates margins and automatically bids on sports cards.
prompt_en: Help me build a small tool that scans eBay for [type of item, e.g. sports cards] listings ending soon, pulls recent sold prices for comparison, and calculates my expected margin after fees and shipping. It should output a ranked list of listings worth bidding on, with my max bid for each based on a [target margin]% margin. Do not place any real bids; show me the list and wait for my go-ahead.

title_zh: Book travel with an AI agent
summary_zh: An author tested AI booking agents for travel; one ticket booking stalled at a human check and the agent asked for help. Another agent can rebook trips and apply credits.
prompt_en: Help me book [flight/train/hotel] from [origin] to [destination] on [dates] for [number] travelers, with a budget of [amount] and preferences of [seat, airline, times, etc.]. Search a few sites, then show me the best 2-3 options with prices and conditions. Pause and show me the full details before entering any payment info or confirming a booking, and if you hit a human check or login, stop and ask me to take over.

title_zh: Draft B2B partnership outreach emails that don't sound like AI
summary_zh: A poster used Claude for partnership outreach, having it flag what sounded like a cold email, and says their reply rate improved.
prompt_en: I'm writing a partnership outreach email to [type of company/role] about [partnership idea]. Here is my draft: [paste draft]. Rewrite it so it sounds like a real person wrote it, and first flag any phrases that sound like a generic cold email or AI-written text and explain why. Give me two final versions of under [100] words each, with a clear, low-pressure ask at the end.

title_zh: Plan and price a full trip through a booking CLI
summary_zh: An AI agent with no prior knowledge of the tooling planned and priced a Dulles–Barcelona round trip with seven hotel nights in under three minutes, verified bookable by dry run (vendor demo).
prompt_en: Plan a round trip from [home airport] to [destination city] leaving [start date] and returning [end date], with [number] hotel nights. Find flight and hotel options within a budget of [amount], and give me a single priced itinerary with links so I can check each part is bookable. Stop once you've presented the itinerary and total cost; do not book or enter payment details without showing me exactly what you're about to purchase and getting my approval.

title_zh: Run marketing research, content and campaigns with Claude
summary_zh: Marketers use Claude Code for competitive analysis, blog drafts, landing pages and HubSpot setup, and Cowork for a team that watches social channels and drafts brand-voice replies.
prompt_en: I do marketing for [company/product]. Research our top [number] competitors [competitor names or websites], then write a competitive analysis summary and a first-draft blog post on [topic] in our brand voice, which is [describe voice]. Save everything as files in this folder and stop when I have the analysis and the draft; before publishing or sending anything or changing any account settings, show me what you plan to do and wait for my approval.

title_zh: Generate ad reports and recommendations from ads data
summary_zh: A commenter connects Claude through an MCP connector to Meta, Google and TikTok ads so it produces reports and recommendations for performance marketing.
prompt_en: Using my connected ad accounts on [Meta, Google, TikTok] for [date range], create a performance report covering spend, results, cost per result and the top and bottom campaigns for [goal, e.g. leads or sales]. Then give me [number] specific recommendations on what to change, with the data behind each. Stop once the report and recommendations are written, and do not change any budgets, ads or settings in the accounts.

title_zh: Build a researched monthly social media calendar
summary_zh: A Claude Code skill researches competitors and communities, then generates 20 posts and 4 video reels in a styled Excel file for up to 12 platforms.
prompt_en: Build me a monthly social media content calendar for [brand/business] in [industry] for [month]. Research [3-5 competitors] and communities like [subreddits, groups or hashtags] to see what resonates, then create an Excel file with [number] posts and [number] short video reel ideas for [platforms], including caption, format and suggested posting date. Stop when the spreadsheet is saved in this folder and give me a short summary of the themes you chose.

title_zh: Run a realtor's Facebook page with a scheduling agent
summary_zh: An agent built for a realtor automatically schedules Facebook posts, and the builders also ran it on their own marketing while handling Meta API permission changes and retries.
prompt_en: Set up an agent that takes the posts I add to [spreadsheet or Google Doc] for my [business type] and schedules them on my Facebook Page [page name] at [days and times]. If a post fails, have it retry [number] times and then email me at [email] with the reason. Before turning it on, show me the schedule and the first post it will publish and wait for my approval.

title_zh: Query the ATS and draft intakes and phone screens
summary_zh: A recruiter uses Claude connected to their ATS to answer queries, create job-specific manager intakes, and draft phone screens per job and candidate.
prompt_en: Using my connected ATS, answer this question: [e.g. which open roles have candidates stuck in screening for over 14 days]. Then for the role [job title], draft a hiring manager intake questionnaire and a phone screen script tailored to the job requirements and to [candidate name or profile]. You're done when I have the answer and both drafts; don't send anything or change any records in the ATS.

title_zh: Draft personalized recruiting outreach and find candidates
summary_zh: A founder gives Claude a job description and has it draft personalized outreach messages and help find candidates.
prompt_en: Here is the job description for [role] at [company]: [paste description]. Draft [number] personalized outreach messages to candidates matching this role, using these profiles or details: [paste candidate info], and suggest where and how to find more people like them. Stop when the drafts and sourcing suggestions are ready; do not send any message.

title_zh: Email authorized Xero invoices to clients automatically
summary_zh: A poster builds a Claude Code workflow that watches for a Xero invoice moving from draft to authorized, saves the PDF, and emails it to the client.
prompt_en: Build me a workflow that checks my Xero account every [15 minutes] for invoices that have just moved from draft to authorized. For each one, download the invoice PDF, save it to [folder path], and write an email to the client's contact address with a short friendly note and the PDF attached. Do not send any email yet: show me the draft and recipient for each invoice and wait for my approval, and stop once you've shown me a working run on [one test invoice].

title_zh: Spot issues in routine contracts with legal AI tools
summary_zh: A commenter uses legal AI tools like Spellbook and CoCounsel to review standard-form contracts and spot issues before deciding whether a specialist is needed.
prompt_en: I'm going to paste a standard-form [type of contract, e.g. NDA, vendor agreement, lease] and I'm on the [party, e.g. customer, tenant] side. Review it clause by clause and flag anything unusual, one-sided, missing, or risky, and rate each issue as low, medium, or high. Finish with a short list of the issues that would justify paying a specialist lawyer to look, and the questions I should ask them. Note that you are not a substitute for legal advice.

title_zh: Assist a home sale and purchase with Claude
summary_zh: A homeowner used Claude to choose agents, analyze the market, track key dates, review contracts, and prepare mortgage documentation.
prompt_en: I'm selling my home at [address] and buying a new one in [area], with a target timeline of [dates]. Help me with each stage: compare real estate agents using these notes [paste notes], summarize the market from these comps [paste data], build a calendar of key dates and deadlines, flag unusual or risky clauses in the contracts I paste in, and list the mortgage documents I need to gather. Finish with a one-page checklist and timeline I can follow, and don't treat anything as legal advice without telling me what to confirm with my agent or attorney.

title_zh: Run equity research on a stock with Claude's plug-in
summary_zh: A poster ran all nine commands of Claude's equity research plug-in on a stock they were researching, testing it as a financial analyst-style tool.
prompt_en: Using the equity research plug-in, run every available command on [ticker or company name], including [list commands if you know them, or say all of them]. When you finish, give me a single summary with the bull case, bear case, key risks, valuation takeaways, and any claims you couldn't verify from sources. Mark clearly where the data may be outdated or missing.

title_zh: Score Reddit investing picks blind on reasoning quality
summary_zh: Built a multi-agent pipeline with Claude Code that pulled 547 r/ValueInvesting recommendations and scored them on reasoning quality without popularity signals.
prompt_en: Build a pipeline that collects the last [500] stock recommendation posts from [subreddit] and strips out upvotes, comment counts, usernames, and any other popularity signals. Then have separate agents score each pick blind on reasoning quality using this rubric: [e.g., thesis clarity, evidence, risk acknowledgment, valuation logic]. When done, save a ranked CSV and a short report on what the top-scored picks had in common, and show me the rubric and a sample of scores before running the full batch.

title_zh: Turn bank statements into a Notion expense database
summary_zh: An agent takes dumped bank statements, asks about unclear transactions, then updates the user's expenses database in Notion.
prompt_en: I'm putting my bank statements in [folder path]. Read them, pull out each transaction, and categorize it using these categories: [list categories]. If a transaction is unclear, ask me about it before assigning a category. Once everything is categorized, show me a preview of the rows you plan to add to my Notion expenses database [database name], and wait for my approval before writing anything to Notion.

title_zh: Send a weekly competitor intelligence digest
summary_zh: A Claude Code skill collects competitor info from websites, founder LinkedIn pages, review sites and ad libraries, then sends a digest every Monday morning.
prompt_en: Build me a reusable skill that tracks these competitors: [competitor names and URLs]. Each run should check their websites, pricing pages, [LinkedIn pages], review sites like [G2 or Capterra] and ad libraries for changes since last time, then write a one-page digest with the top changes and what I should do about them. Save it as a file in [folder]; before setting up any scheduled send or emailing it, show me the draft and the recipient list and wait for my okay.

title_zh: Turn lesson notes into tailored student feedback documents
summary_zh: A language teacher uses an AI agent to turn notes into a formatted feedback document with corrections, explanations and homework tailored to each student's errors.
prompt_en: I teach [language] to [level] students. Here are my lesson notes for [student name]: [paste notes with their errors and topics covered]. Write a formatted feedback document with their corrections, a short clear explanation of each mistake, and 5 to 8 homework exercises targeting those specific errors. Keep the tone [encouraging/direct], and finish with the document ready to copy into [Google Docs/Word].

title_zh: Build a translation agent for text, URLs and files
summary_zh: The author used Claude Code to build, with no hand-written code, an agent that translates text, a URL or a local file; it fetched a blog's articles and translated two into Chinese.
prompt_en: Build me a small translation tool that takes either pasted text, a URL, or a local file path and translates it into [target language]. Fetch the page or read the file, keep the original formatting and headings, and save the result as [output file name]. Test it by translating [a sample URL or file] and show me the result, then tell me how to run it myself.

title_zh: Run an e-commerce store with a human-approved agent
summary_zh: An agent operates the author's own store, handling inventory monitoring, support triage, sales anomaly detection and review summaries, with human approval for money or high-stakes customer matters.
prompt_en: Set up an agent for my online store on [Shopify/WooCommerce/other] that checks [inventory levels daily], sorts incoming support emails into [categories like shipping, refunds, product questions], flags unusual sales spikes or drops, and sends me a weekly summary of new reviews. It may draft replies and reports on its own, but it must pause and ask me before issuing refunds, changing prices, or replying to angry or high-stakes customers. Show me a test run on [last week's data] so I can confirm it works.

title_zh: Track tasks, research ideas and review crypto history with Grok Bot
summary_zh: The poster uses Grok Bot to sort and track tasks, research business ideas, help with YouTube editing and make sense of four years of Binance history.
prompt_en: Help me organize my life and projects. Sort this list of tasks into priorities and set up a simple tracker I can check each day: [paste tasks]. Then research [business idea] and give me a one-page summary of the market, competitors, and a first step, and go through my exported [exchange name] transaction history in [file] to summarize my trades, gains and losses by year. Don't take any actions on my accounts, just report.

title_zh: Hand routine browser tasks to Grok Bot
summary_zh: A user has Grok Bot use the computer for browser tasks that can't be done directly; it handled routine ones for weeks before later refusing some.
prompt_en: Use your computer's browser to do this routine task for me: [describe task, e.g., download the monthly report from site X and save it to a folder]. Repeat it [daily/weekly] and tell me when each run finishes with a short summary of what you did. Pause and show me what you're about to do before submitting any form, making a payment, sending a message, or deleting anything.

title_zh: Run solopreneur admin workflows with Grok Bot
summary_zh: A solopreneur used Grok Bot for business workflows and administrative work until a later update made it worse.
prompt_en: I run a one-person business doing [what you do]. Take over these admin workflows: [invoicing, scheduling, inbox triage, customer follow-ups]. Draft everything first and show me before sending any email, invoice, or payment, and finish each run with a short list of what is done and what needs my decision.

title_zh: Get hands-free recipes while cooking
summary_zh: A commenter uses Grok through AirPods while cooking so they don't have to look at their phone for recipes.
prompt_en: I'm cooking [dish] right now and have my hands full, so talk me through the recipe by voice, one step at a time. Wait for me to say 'next' before moving on, and answer questions like substitutions or timing as they come up. I have [ingredients on hand] and need it ready in [time], and the job is done when the dish is plated.

title_zh: Have Grok Bot read reports and suggest next steps
summary_zh: A commenter checks messages from Grok Bot after it reads reports and suggests the next step; another let it do all the coding but hit weekly limits quickly.
prompt_en: Every [morning/week], read the reports I put in [folder or inbox location] and send me a short message with the key points and the one next step you recommend. If a report needs a decision from me, say so clearly at the top. Don't send anything to other people or change any files without showing me first.

title_zh: Research your family tree with Claude Code
summary_zh: The author used Claude Code to do genealogical research and map out multiple branches of their family tree using digitized records.
prompt_en: I want to research my family tree starting with [your name, birth year, and what you know about parents and grandparents, including places and approximate dates]. Search freely available digitized records such as [FamilySearch, national archives, census or immigration databases] and build a folder of notes with one file per person, citing the source for every fact. Mark anything uncertain as unverified rather than guessing, and finish with a summary file mapping each branch and listing the best next gaps to research.

title_zh: Run a personal assistant that handles email and books group outings
summary_zh: A user's week with Muse: it checked inboxes, drafted replies, booked a bowling night for four in Toronto and tracked split payments; doctor portal booking hit limits.
prompt_en: Act as my personal assistant this week. Check my inbox and draft replies to anything that needs one, but show me the drafts before sending. Then plan a [activity, e.g. bowling] night for [number] people in [city] on [date range], find a venue with availability, and track who owes what for the split. Pause and show me the details before booking anything or sending any messages, and finish with a summary of what is done and what is still open.

title_zh: Triage unread email hourly and send Monday briefings
summary_zh: The writer says Muse scans unread email hourly, ranks it by importance, and sends Monday briefings; an early mistake archiving a promo was corrected.
prompt_en: Every hour, scan my unread email and rank it by importance: needs a reply today, needs a reply this week, and can wait. Every Monday at [time], send me a briefing with the top items, upcoming deadlines, and anything waiting on someone else. Do not archive or delete anything without asking me first; instead list what you would archive and let me approve it.

title_zh: Give an agent its own email to finish sign-ups
summary_zh: The poster gave Muse its own email address so it can complete account sign-ups and handle verification emails without stalling.
prompt_en: I need to sign up for [service or website] using the dedicated email address [agent email address]. Fill out the sign-up form, then open that inbox, find the verification email, and complete confirmation. Pause and show me the details before submitting anything that involves payment or personal information, and stop once the account is verified and I can log in.

title_zh: Book flights with an agent (with a failed email entry)
summary_zh: One commenter had Muse book flights but it entered the email wrong, so no confirmation arrived; a partial success.
prompt_en: Find and book a flight from [origin] to [destination] departing [date] and returning [date] for [number] traveler(s), with a budget of [price] and preference for [nonstop, time of day, airline]. Use my email [email] for the confirmation. Before entering payment details or finalizing, pause and show me the itinerary, price, and the email address you typed so I can check it, then confirm that a confirmation page appeared.

title_zh: Run an agent swarm attempting to solve P vs. NP
summary_zh: A swarm of AI agents works on the P vs. NP problem, with progress shown on a live dashboard.
prompt_en: Set up a small swarm of sub-agents to work on [a hard open problem, e.g. a specific NP-hard problem or a restricted case of P vs. NP]. Have each sub-agent try a different approach, such as [approach 1], [approach 2], and [approach 3], and write its findings and any checkable proofs or counterexamples to a shared folder. Build a simple local dashboard page showing each agent's status and results, and stop after [number] rounds with a summary of what was tried, what failed, and what looks promising, being clear about anything unverified.

title_zh: Mark old Gmail emails as read with an agent
summary_zh: A user asked ChatGPT Agent Mode with a Gmail connector to mark emails before a date as read; it was unclear if it finished and the agent's status was inconsistent.
prompt_en: Using my connected Gmail, find all emails in my inbox received before [date] that are unread and mark them as read. First tell me how many emails match and show me a few examples, then wait for my go-ahead before changing anything. When finished, report the final count marked as read and confirm that no unread emails before [date] remain, or tell me clearly what could not be completed.

title_zh: Collect receipts for expense reimbursements
summary_zh: The poster used OpenClaw to gather receipts for several trip reimbursements, saving them quite some time.
prompt_en: I took [number] trips for work between [start date] and [end date]. Search my email at [email account] and any folders I point you to for receipts from those trips, save each one into a folder named [trip name] with the date, vendor, and amount in the filename, and give me a spreadsheet totaling each trip. You're done when every trip has its receipts and a total, and you've flagged any that look missing. Don't submit anything to my employer's expense system; show me the finished package first.

title_zh: Monitor feeds for story angles and draft content
summary_zh: A commenter's OpenClaw watches Reddit and news for story angles, drafts content, logs to memory, and pings Telegram, cutting 2-3 hours of work to about 20 minutes of review.
prompt_en: Every [morning/hour] check [subreddits and news sites] for new stories related to [my topic or beat] and pick the [3-5] with the strongest angles for my audience of [audience]. For each one, write a short draft in my voice ([tone description]) and save it to your memory log so you don't repeat topics. Then send me a summary of the picks on [Telegram/other chat app]. Never publish or post anything; drafts only, for me to review.

title_zh: Plan and book a New Zealand South Island trip
summary_zh: The poster used OpenClaw and Claude Code to plan a South Island trip; the agent handled much of the booking work, though they still made 12 of 13 bookings themselves.
prompt_en: Help me plan a [number]-day trip to [destination] from [start date] to [end date] for [number of travelers], with a budget of [amount] and interests in [interests]. Create a day-by-day itinerary in a file, plus a checklist of every booking I need (flights, lodging, car, activities) with links, prices, and cancellation terms. You're done when the checklist is complete and ordered by what to book first. Don't book or pay for anything; pause and show me the details before any purchase step.

title_zh: Script image metadata tagging and Photoshop embedding
summary_zh: A commenter had Claude write scripts that scan images, write metadata, and embed it in Photoshop, building a batch web-image mockup tool.
prompt_en: Write me a script that scans the images in [folder path], generates a descriptive title, caption, and keywords for each one, and writes them into the file's metadata. Then add a step that [embeds or uses this metadata in Photoshop/another tool] for a batch mockup of [web page or layout]. Test it on [3] copies of my images first and show me the results. Only run it on the full folder after I approve, and never overwrite the originals.

title_zh: Schedule weekly internet research summaries
summary_zh: The poster is building a Cowork agent that collects research online and summarizes it, and is working out how to schedule it weekly.
prompt_en: Every [day] at [time], research the latest news and publications on [topic] from [preferred sources or websites], and write a one-page summary covering the [5] most important findings with links. Save it to [folder] as a dated file and include a short list of questions worth following up. Run it once now so I can check the format, and then set it up to repeat weekly. Don't email or share it with anyone without asking me.

title_zh: Explain a denied insurance claim from EOB and policy
summary_zh: Claude Code cross-referenced an EOB and policy documents in about three minutes and showed the author owed nothing beyond what they already paid; it did not file anything.
prompt_en: I'm putting my Explanation of Benefits at [path to EOB file] and my policy documents in [folder path] in the same folder. Read them and explain why this claim was denied or reduced, what I actually owe, and whether the amount matches my plan's deductible, copay and coinsurance. Give me a short plain-English summary plus the exact policy language you relied on, and do not contact anyone or file anything.

title_zh: Audit vendor dashboard paths and correct stale docs
summary_zh: Claude in Chrome walked 106 dashboard paths read-only across the poster's Stripe, Cloudflare, Supabase and GitHub accounts, and eight changed paths were corrected in the records.
prompt_en: Go through this list of dashboard paths for my [Stripe, Cloudflare, Supabase, GitHub] accounts, which is in [paste the list or doc]. Open each one in read-only mode, never click save, delete or change any setting, and tell me whether the path still works and matches what my docs say. A finished job is a table of each path with its status, and a list of corrected paths for the docs. Show me the corrections before you edit anything.

title_zh: Bulk upload documents to a website via browser agent
summary_zh: The poster pairs Claude Desktop for file management with Claude in Chrome to upload many documents to a website.
prompt_en: I have a folder of documents at [folder path] that need to go to [website name and upload page URL]. Sort the files by [name, date or category], then upload them one by one in the browser, matching each to the right field or folder on the site. Before you submit anything, show me the full list of what will be uploaded where and wait for my approval. When done, give me a checklist of what succeeded and what failed.

title_zh: Diagnose and clean up a slow Windows PC
summary_zh: Users had Claude connect to Task Manager, diagnose performance problems, and guide them through the fixes to get their computer running well again.
prompt_en: My Windows PC has been running slowly, especially when I [describe, such as starting up or opening many tabs]. Help me diagnose it by walking me through what to check in Task Manager, such as CPU, memory, disk and startup apps, and tell me what each reading means. Then give me step-by-step fixes ranked by impact, and ask me to confirm before any step that deletes files or uninstalls software.

title_zh: Automate video editing on a personal PC
summary_zh: A user films clips on their phone, sends them to their computer, and Claude runs the editing pipeline without an editing app or MCP plugin.
prompt_en: I film short clips on my phone and move them to [folder path] on my computer. Set up a repeatable pipeline using free command-line tools like ffmpeg that takes the clips in that folder and produces one finished video with [trims, cuts, captions, music, resolution]. A finished job is one script I can run on a new folder of clips, and a sample output from my current files. Never overwrite the original clips.

title_zh: Handle client Jira tickets and fixes with Claude
summary_zh: A developer has Claude Code reply to client Jira tickets and fix issues from the client's feedback, with the client believing they are talking to the human developer.
prompt_en: Here are the ticket details and my repo at [path]. Read the ticket [ticket ID or pasted text], find the cause in the code, implement a fix, and run the tests. Then draft a clear, professional reply for me to send back to the client explaining what changed. Show me the diff and the draft reply, and wait for my approval before committing, pushing or posting anything.

title_zh: Control agent sessions across computers from mobile
summary_zh: A commenter used Claude to build a mobile app, plus a Mac app for handoff, to control agent sessions across multiple computers.
prompt_en: Help me build a small mobile-friendly web app, plus a simple desktop companion for [Mac or Windows], that lets me see and control my coding agent sessions running on [number] computers. It should list active sessions per machine, show their latest output, and let me send a new instruction from my phone. Start with a plan and an architecture I can run on my own network, then build the first working version that connects two machines.

title_zh: Run an agency's work through many Claude Code sessions
summary_zh: A small agency owner uses Claude Code for nearly everything, running many long-lived sessions across projects on the machines where the work lives.
prompt_en: I run a small [type of agency] and want to manage my work through Claude Code sessions, one per project. Help me set up a folder structure for [list of 3 projects], with a short instruction file in each that describes the client, goals, tone, and rules about what you may and may not do. Then start a session for [project name] and complete this task: [describe task]. Pause before sending anything to a client or deleting any file.

title_zh: Order a pizza to your house with an agent
summary_zh: A writer asked ChatGPT Agent to find a well-rated local pizza place and order; it clicked through pop-ups, couldn't reach the order section, and gave up.
prompt_en: Find a well-rated [cuisine, e.g. pizza] place near [my address or neighborhood] that is open now and delivers. Open its ordering page and build an order for [items and quantities]. If a pop-up or page blocks you from reaching the menu, tell me where you got stuck instead of looping. Stop before payment and show me the restaurant, items, delivery fee, and total so I can approve.

title_zh: Turn saved recipes into a weekly meal plan and carts
summary_zh: A Claude Code skill using Claude in Chrome turns saved Pinterest and Instagram recipes into a plan, checks budget, then fills Whole Foods and Instacart carts after approval without checking out.
prompt_en: Take the recipes I saved in [Pinterest board or Instagram collection link] and pick [number] for this week's dinners for [number] people. Combine the ingredients into one shopping list, check it against my budget of [$ amount], and show me the plan. After I approve it, fill my [Whole Foods or Instacart] cart in the browser, then stop and don't check out.

title_zh: Produce a short film end to end with an agent
summary_zh: The poster says Claude Code wrote the script, voiced lines with a local TTS model, made the music, rendered frames in headless Chrome, and mixed it with ffmpeg.
prompt_en: Help me make a [length, e.g. 60-second] short film about [premise] in the folder [path]. Write the script, generate voiceover with a local text-to-speech tool, create or source background music, render the visuals as frames, and assemble everything with ffmpeg. Finish with one playable file named [filename] and a short note on how to re-render it.

title_zh: Run a solo SaaS with an agent that texts you
summary_zh: A solo founder of a hosted SaaS has Claude Code write most code and text them when it needs input, taking instructions by phone.
prompt_en: Work on my codebase at [path] to ship [feature or bug list], and run the tests as you go. When you need a decision or hit something you can't resolve, send me a short message at [text or chat channel] with your question and options, then wait for my reply. Finish each task with a summary of changes and a branch or pull request, and don't deploy to production without my approval.

title_zh: Open every AI story from a news homepage in tabs
summary_zh: A Comet user had it open The Verge's homepage and open all AI stories in new tabs, and also reported it handling email, LinkedIn messages and Reddit posts.
prompt_en: Open [news site homepage URL] and find every story about [topic, e.g. AI] currently on the page. Open each one in its own new tab, skipping duplicates, videos, and sponsored posts. When done, tell me how many tabs you opened and list the headlines in the order of the tabs.

title_zh: Fill forms and scan Marketplace with a browser agent
summary_zh: A user used Comet to fill forms, complete compliance trainings, and scan Facebook Marketplace, though it recently began refusing those agentic tasks.
prompt_en: Open [website or form URL] and fill out the form using these details: [your info]. Stop on the final page before submitting and show me everything you entered so I can confirm. Separately, scan [marketplace site] for [item] within [distance] of [location] under $[price] and list the 5 best listings with price, location, and link.

title_zh: Book things with Chrome's Gemini agent
summary_zh: A user had Gemini in Chrome book things for them and used AI to craft prompts and instructions to improve agentic booking.
prompt_en: Use Agent Mode to book [what to book, e.g. a table for 4, a haircut, a hotel night] in [city/location] on [date and time window]. My preferences are [budget, cuisine or style, distance, must-haves]. Compare at least three options, recommend one, and take it through to the final confirmation screen. Pause before entering payment details or pressing the final confirm button so I can review the details, and stop once the booking is confirmed and you've given me the confirmation summary.

title_zh: Control a PC for small tasks with ChatGPT
summary_zh: A user has ChatGPT control their PC to install game mods, update apps, do color correction in DaVinci, and organize files, and asks whether Gemini can do the same.
prompt_en: Take control of my computer and handle these small tasks one at a time: [task 1, e.g. install mods for a game], [task 2, e.g. update my outdated apps], [task 3, e.g. organize my Downloads folder by file type]. Tell me what you plan to do before each task and narrate as you go. Pause and ask me before deleting any files, running installers from unfamiliar sources, or changing system settings, and finish with a short list of what was done and anything that needs my attention.

title_zh: Fill tourist visa applications on government portals
summary_zh: AI agents operate a browser on official government portals to fill visa applications, check documents, and book appointments, with human expert review of each file.
prompt_en: I'm a [your nationality] citizen applying for a [country] [visa type] visa. Go to the official [country] government visa portal, fill in the application using the details I give you, and list every document I need to upload and any appointment slots available near [your city]. Stop and show me the full filled-in form and any fees before you submit anything, pay, or book an appointment.

title_zh: Control Netflix and send messages by voice
summary_zh: A user had Alexa+ find and navigate to an anime on Netflix, announce calendar events, and send emails and texts from simple commands.
prompt_en: Alexa, open Netflix and find [show or movie title], then start [episode or season]. Then read out my calendar events for [today or date], and send a text to [contact name] saying [message]. Read each message back to me and wait for my okay before sending it.

title_zh: Plan meals and order the groceries
summary_zh: A parent used Dot to create meals, build a grocery list, and fill the cart and order through a store app.
prompt_en: Plan [number] dinners for my [household description] for the week of [date], keeping to [dietary needs, budget, and foods we dislike]. Build one combined grocery list, then open my [store name] app and fill the cart with those items, picking [brand or price preferences]. Stop before checkout and show me the cart, substitutions, and total so I can approve the order.

title_zh: Use an agent as a personal assistant that emails family
summary_zh: A user shifted Dot from orchestrator to personal assistant, and it emailed their mum to introduce itself on its own.
prompt_en: Act as my personal assistant. Each morning, review my inbox and calendar, summarize what needs my attention, and draft replies for anything routine. Draft but do not send any email to [family member or contact] until I approve it, and show me the draft first.

title_zh: Automate browser workflows in a cloud browser
summary_zh: A user set up Dot in its cloud browser for autonomous workflows, but it often broke down and asked for repeated logins and permissions.
prompt_en: Using your cloud browser, run this workflow for me: [describe the steps, such as logging into a site, exporting a report, and filling a spreadsheet]. Tell me up front which logins or permissions you need so I can grant them all at once, then carry out the task and report what you did. Pause and show me before you submit any form, send anything, or delete anything.

title_zh: Manage Plex and schedule data-scraping cron jobs
summary_zh: A user has Hermes Agent help manage Plex and set up cron jobs that scrape and archive data.
prompt_en: Help me manage my Plex server at [server address or host]. First review the library and tell me what needs attention, such as [missing metadata, duplicate files, storage use]. Then set up a cron job that runs [script or command] on [schedule] to scrape and archive [data source] into [folder path], with logs I can check. Show me the exact crontab entry and the script before you install them, and do not delete any existing files. Stop when a test run succeeds and you have explained how to check it.

title_zh: Revive old MacBook Airs as headless Mac mini extensions
summary_zh: A user had Hermes Agent help turn two old MacBook Air laptops into headless extensions of a Mac mini and asked it for directive text for each agent.
prompt_en: I want to turn my old [laptop model] into a headless extension of my [main computer, e.g. Mac mini]. Walk me through the setup step by step, covering remote access, auto-login, sleep settings, and how the machines share work, and tell me what to run on each one. Then write a short directive text for the agent on each machine describing its role: [role of main machine], [role of laptop 1], [role of laptop 2]. Pause and show me any command that changes system settings or erases data before running it. You are done when I can reach each laptop remotely and each agent has its directive.

title_zh: Run a trading agent team and build decks with a script
summary_zh: A user organizes a trading setup with an orchestrator and sub-agents for analysis and debate, and had Hermes write a Python script to build decks, though it got confused by direct file edits.
prompt_en: Help me set up a team of agents for [analysis task, e.g. evaluating stocks I am watching]: one orchestrator and sub-agents for [analysis], [bull case], and [bear case] who debate before the orchestrator summarizes. Then write a Python script that builds a slide deck from the summary at [output path], and have the script generate the files rather than editing existing files directly. Do not place any trades or connect to any brokerage account. The job is finished when I can run the script and get a deck for [ticker or topic].

title_zh: Let an AI agent read and draft replies in your inbox
summary_zh: An author ran an agent on his professional inbox for a week to read, draft and send email in his voice; it guessed wrongly on one reply, so he kept it in draft mode.
prompt_en: Go through my inbox for [email account] over the last [number] days and read every message that needs a reply. For each one, write a draft reply in my voice, using my past sent emails as a guide, and save it as a draft only. Do not send anything; when you are finished, give me a list of the drafts and flag any where you had to guess at facts, dates or commitments.

title_zh: Run a personal assistant over an Obsidian vault
summary_zh: An OpenClaw agent connected to her Obsidian vault sends a daily agenda, checks progress, and creates or reschedules tasks and marks habits via Discord.
prompt_en: Connect to my Obsidian vault at [vault path] and my [Discord/chat app]. Every morning at [time], send me an agenda built from my tasks and notes, and check in on progress in the evening. When I message you, create or reschedule tasks and mark habits done in the vault; ask me before you delete or overwrite any note.

title_zh: Build and launch a market research SaaS with Replit
summary_zh: The poster used Replit's agent to help build a market research SaaS and made a first sale after months of weekend work.
prompt_en: Help me build a [type of product, e.g. market research tool] web app for [target customer]. Start by proposing the core features and a simple first version I can show people, then build it step by step with sign-up, [key feature] and a way to take payment. Pause and ask me before you connect any payment account or publish it live.

title_zh: Build an exam-marking app for a hackathon
summary_zh: The poster built a mobile web app that scans exam papers and marks them with AI using Replit Agent, winning $10,000 for about $15 in credits over 22 hours.
prompt_en: Build a mobile-friendly web app that lets me [scan/upload] [type of document, e.g. exam papers] with my phone camera and uses AI to [mark/grade/summarize] them against [answer key or rubric]. Finish when I can upload a sample document and see a score with a short explanation for each answer. Ask me before you publish it or connect any paid API keys.

title_zh: Write a Forth implementation for the PDP-7
summary_zh: A retired engineer used Claude to write a Forth for the PDP-7 in one morning, including a turtle graphics library and an assembler for the Type 340 display.
prompt_en: I want to write a [language or tool, e.g. Forth interpreter] for [vintage or unusual machine, e.g. PDP-7] in [assembly or host language]. Start by asking me for the instruction set docs or an emulator I have, then build it in small steps, running tests after each one. Finish with a working core plus one demo program like [e.g. turtle graphics], and a short README explaining how to build and run it.

title_zh: Handle patient calls for appointments, bills and refills
summary_zh: MUSC Health's voice agent Emily handles 25% of patient calls, booking appointments, taking bill payments and processing prescription refill requests.
prompt_en: Build me a phone assistant for [clinic or office name] that answers patient calls, books or reschedules appointments in [scheduling system], and logs refill requests for staff to review. It should answer billing questions using [billing info source] but must not take payments or submit refills itself. It should pass any call it cannot handle to [staff phone or email]. Before turning it on, show me the call flow and a sample test call for me to approve.

title_zh: Run a local business's WhatsApp orders with an AI assistant
summary_zh: Built in n8n for a paying client: transcribes voice notes, analyzes images, and hands buying intent to an order-execution agent.
prompt_en: Help me build an n8n workflow for [business name] that receives incoming WhatsApp messages. It should transcribe voice notes, describe any images, and work out whether the customer wants to buy [products]. If so, it should pass the order details to a second agent that prepares the order in [order system]. Pause for my approval before placing any order or sending any reply to a customer. You're done when a test voice note and a test photo each produce the correct order summary.

title_zh: Check appointment availability through a booking chatbot
summary_zh: An n8n chatbot workflow has a booking agent that calls another workflow to check appointment availability in Booksy.
prompt_en: Help me build an n8n chatbot for [business name] that answers customer questions and, when someone asks about an appointment, calls a separate workflow to check open slots in [booking system, e.g. Booksy] for [service] on [date range]. It should reply with the available times. It should not book anything until the customer confirms and I have reviewed the booking step. You're done when a test chat returns real availability.

title_zh: Turn tagged Readwise articles into Notion summaries
summary_zh: A Zapier Agent reads an article in Readwise Reader, reviews the user's highlights, and drafts a summary into a Notion database when a specific tag is applied.
prompt_en: Create a Zapier Agent that triggers when I add the tag [tag name] to an article in Readwise Reader. It should read the article and my highlights, then draft a summary of [length] that reflects the points I highlighted and add it to my Notion database [database name]. Include the title, link and tags in the Notion entry. You're done when a test article with the tag produces a correct Notion page, and show me the draft before the first save.

title_zh: Send and split money by chatting with your AI agent
summary_zh: An MCP in front of a wallet lets an agent send and request money, split dinners, trips and poker ledgers, with passkey approval or preset trusted contacts.
prompt_en: Connect to my [wallet or payments MCP] and help me split [a dinner / a trip / a poker night] with [names of people]. Work out who owes what from these details: [amounts, who paid, any exceptions]. Show me the full list of requests or payments, with names and amounts, and wait for my approval before sending or requesting any money. You're done when I've confirmed and each person has a request or payment queued.

title_zh: Route refused tasks between local and frontier models
summary_zh: A commenter runs a local Qwen model with an agents.md policy that escalates refused tasks via a shared SQL task board to a model willing to do them, such as clicking login buttons.
prompt_en: Help me set up a routing policy between my local model [model name, e.g. Qwen] and a stronger hosted model. Write an agents.md that tells the local model to log any task it refuses or can't do into a shared SQL task board table at [database path], with fields for task, status and result. Then write a small worker that picks up those pending tasks and sends them to [hosted model]. Run one test task and show me the board before and after. Ask me before running anything that touches my accounts.

title_zh: Have an AI agent shop for a gift on a $25 budget
summary_zh: The author gave an agent a virtual debit card to buy a gift; it browsed, compared products and reached checkout but struggled with CAPTCHAs, dynamic pricing and bot-blocking stores.
prompt_en: Find a gift for [recipient, with their interests] under $[25] total including shipping and tax. Browse a few stores, compare at least [3] options on price, reviews and delivery time, and recommend one with reasons. Take it to the checkout page but stop before entering payment details or placing the order, and show me the item, final price and shipping address for approval. If a store blocks you or shows a CAPTCHA, skip it and tell me which one.

title_zh: Let Google AI Mode find and check out a gift
summary_zh: A reporter set a target price and permission to buy for a haircare gift set; Google opened a prefilled checkout and also called nearby stores to check stock.
prompt_en: Find [a specific gift, e.g. a haircare gift set for a friend with curly hair] and buy it only if the total comes to $[target price] or less. Check a few retailers, including whether [nearby stores or my city] have it in stock, and call stores if needed. Open the prefilled checkout and stop there, showing me the item, price, shipping and payment method before I approve the purchase.

title_zh: Mass-apply to jobs with customized cover letters
summary_zh: A job seeker used Grok to tailor hand-written cover letters to roles matching at least 50% of requirements and send general outreach otherwise, reporting 800+ applications and 6 interviews.
prompt_en: I'm looking for [job title] roles in [location or remote]. Find openings on [job boards], and for each one compare the requirements to my resume at [link or pasted text]. If I match at least 50% of the requirements, tailor my cover letter from [my sample letter] to that role; otherwise draft a short general outreach note to the hiring contact. Put every opening, match score, and draft in a spreadsheet, and pause to show me the first five drafts before sending or submitting anything.

title_zh: Prep outbound sales work with a coding agent
summary_zh: An outbound practitioner uses Claude Code for call prep, tradeshow workflows, account list building, ICP/TAM analysis, CSV cleaning, scraping, and built a custom CRM lookup app.
prompt_en: I do outbound sales for [product] aimed at [ideal customer]. Take this file of accounts, [CSV path], then clean the data, remove duplicates, and score each account against my ICP: [ICP criteria]. For the top [number] accounts, write a one-page call prep brief covering what the company does, likely pain points, and two opening questions. Save the cleaned CSV and the briefs in a new folder, and do not change my original file.

title_zh: Call doctors' offices and book the earliest in-network appointment
summary_zh: An AI agent phones offices for the user to find the earliest in-network slot and book specialists, dentists, follow-ups, or new primary care visits.
prompt_en: Find the earliest in-network appointment for [type: specialist, dentist, follow-up, or new primary care] near [my city/zip] with my insurance [plan name]. Check each practice's availability online and call them if I've enabled phone calls, then list the top [3] options with date, time, address, and phone number. Before booking or sharing my date of birth, member ID, or any personal details, pause and show me what you're about to send. You're done when I've approved one option and you've confirmed the booking.

title_zh: Create an AWS account with a coding agent
summary_zh: The author had Claude Code set up their AWS account, aiming to smooth the onboarding that newcomers usually struggle with.
prompt_en: Walk me through creating and securing a new AWS account for [my purpose, e.g. a side project]. Use the AWS CLI where you can, and give me exact steps for anything I must do in the browser, like identity verification or payment details. Finish when I have a non-root admin user with MFA, a budget alert set at [amount], and the CLI working with a test command. Pause and show me before running any command that creates billable resources or changes billing settings.

title_zh: Run Lighthouse SEO audits and fix a site with an agent
summary_zh: An agent using chrome-devtools-mcp ran Lighthouse on the author's site, applied fixes, and re-audited to reach 100 on Accessibility and SEO.
prompt_en: Using chrome-devtools-mcp, run a Lighthouse audit on [my site URL] and list every Accessibility and SEO issue it finds. Fix the issues in my codebase at [project folder], then re-run the audit to confirm. Stop when Accessibility and SEO both score 100 or you've listed what's blocking it, and show me a summary of the changes before committing anything.

title_zh: Find unclaimed government money and negotiate bills
summary_zh: A founder pitches a background agent that searches for unclaimed government money under a user's name and negotiates bills to save money.
prompt_en: Search official unclaimed property databases, such as [my state's site] and the national lookup, for money under the name [full name], including past names [former names] and past addresses [cities]. Give me a list of each match with the amount, holder, and claim link. Don't submit any claim forms or enter my personal ID details; pause and show me before taking any such step.

title_zh: Search unclaimed property for family members
summary_zh: A commenter says Grok Bot's unclaimed-property search found money for their mom and uncle.
prompt_en: Search unclaimed property databases, such as [state sites] and the national lookup, for [family member's full name], with past names [names] and past cities [cities]. Report each match with the amount, holder, and official claim link. I'm checking on behalf of family with their permission. Don't submit any claim or enter sensitive info; pause and show me before taking any such step.

title_zh: Find a 1952 paper solving a modeling sub-problem
summary_zh: A researcher developing a model had Claude Code point them to a 1952 paper with a better steady-state solution than their time-dependent approach.
prompt_en: I'm building a model of [describe your system and what it predicts], and I currently solve it with [your current approach, e.g. a time-dependent simulation]. Search for older or foundational papers, including pre-1980 work, that give a steady-state, analytical, or simpler solution to [the specific sub-problem]. Finish with a list of 3 to 5 candidate papers, each with citation, a two-sentence summary of its method, and how it could replace or improve my current approach.

title_zh: Process vendor invoices with a bookkeeping agent
summary_zh: Two accountants at a $10M firm built an invoice-processing agent with Cursor and Claude Code, reporting cost falling from about $7 to $0.20 per invoice.
prompt_en: I'm an accountant at [firm type] and I want to build an agent that processes vendor invoices from the folder [path to invoice PDFs]. For each invoice, extract vendor, date, invoice number, line items, and total, suggest a GL account from my chart of accounts in [file name], and flag anything unusual like duplicates or missing fields. Write results to a CSV I can review, and stop there; do not post anything to my accounting system or send any messages without showing me first.

title_zh: Build a tax document gathering and bookkeeping workflow
summary_zh: A poster used Claude Code to build a tax document gathering hub, generate bookkeeping reports, and then a full bookkeeping app.
prompt_en: Help me build a tax document gathering workflow for [tax year] in the folder [path]. Create a checklist of the documents I need (such as W-2s, 1099s, receipts, and bank statements) based on my situation: [filing status, income types, deductions]. Then scan the files in the folder, mark which items are present or missing, and produce a simple bookkeeping summary by category. Don't move, rename, or delete any files without showing me the plan first.

title_zh: Optimize code through an automated falsifiable-hypothesis loop
summary_zh: An agent skill profiles code, proposes and tests optimization hypotheses in a loop, keeps verified improvements in version control, and writes a PDF report; it sped up KaHIP 3.9x and VieCut 8.9x.
prompt_en: In my repository at [path or repo], profile [program or benchmark command] and find the biggest performance bottlenecks. Then loop: state a falsifiable hypothesis for a speedup, implement it, run [test command] to confirm correctness and re-run the benchmark, and commit only changes that are verified faster, reverting the rest. Stop after [number] hypotheses or when gains flatten, then write a short PDF report with the baseline, each hypothesis and its result, and the final speedup. Do not push to any remote or delete branches without showing me first.

title_zh: Support academic social science work with a coding agent setup
summary_zh: A social scientist shares a Claude Code configuration they built to support much of their academic work, such as analysis and writing.
prompt_en: Help me set up this folder as a research workspace for my [field, e.g. political science] work. Create a CLAUDE.md that records my conventions: [analysis tools, e.g. R or Python], citation style [style], writing voice [description], and folder layout for data, code, and drafts. Add a few reusable commands for jobs like [e.g. cleaning survey data, running a regression table, editing a paper section]. Finish by walking me through the setup and a test run on [a sample file], and ask before overwriting or deleting any existing file.

title_zh: Build a multi-agent system on AWS
summary_zh: The author built a multi-agent system on AWS as the final project of Udacity's AWS Agent Engineer Nanodegree.
prompt_en: Help me build a small multi-agent system on AWS for [describe the task, e.g. triaging customer support emails]. Start by proposing an architecture with one coordinator agent and [number] specialist agents, and tell me which AWS services each would use. Then scaffold the code in this folder, add a README with deploy steps, and stop once I can run one end-to-end test locally. Pause and show me the plan before you create or change anything in my AWS account.

title_zh: Gate refund actions with a tool-gate model
summary_zh: The author tested Strands Decider 2B as a tool gate that decides whether an agent should act on 16 refund cases, compared against Nova Pro as a judge.
prompt_en: I want to test whether a small model can act as a gate that decides if an agent should take an action like [e.g. issuing a refund]. Write a script that runs [number] test cases from [file or description of cases] through the gate model and through a larger judge model, then compares their decisions. A finished job is a table showing each case, both decisions, where they disagree, and the overall agreement rate. Do not call any real refund or payment systems; use mock tools only.

title_zh: Source motivated-seller real estate deals from Redfin listings
summary_zh: Claude pulls up to 150 active Redfin listings via a scraper, computes median price per square foot, and flags below-median listings with long days on market for investors. Tutorial, not a confirmed first-person account.
prompt_en: Here is a list of up to [150] active real estate listings in [city or zip code] with price, square footage, and days on market: [paste data or attach file]. Calculate the median price per square foot, then flag listings priced below that median that have been on the market more than [60] days. Give me a ranked table of the flagged listings with the reasons they look like motivated sellers, and note any listings with missing data you had to skip.

title_zh: Analyze a rental property deal with comps and rehab costs
summary_zh: Claude Code, connected to an MCP server, pulls property value, comps and rent estimates and runs a deal analysis on a $312,000 Florida listing with $45,000 rehab. Vendor example, not a real user report.
prompt_en: Analyze this rental property deal: [address], listed at $[price] with an estimated $[rehab cost] rehab. Pull the estimated value, comparable sales, and rent estimates from [data source or connected tool], then calculate total investment, projected monthly cash flow, cap rate, and cash-on-cash return using [down payment and interest rate] financing. Finish with a one-page summary and a clear buy, negotiate, or pass recommendation, listing any assumptions you made.

title_zh: Run data research projects with a coding agent
summary_zh: An author used Claude Code on data projects including Canadian daycare research, grading it B- for imperfect reliability and weak research documentation.
