prompt_en: I want to research [topic, e.g. childcare costs in my province] using public data. Find the relevant datasets, download them, clean them, and write analysis scripts that answer [my research question]. Keep a README that records every source, every cleaning step, and any assumption or number you could not verify, so I can check your work. Stop when I have one chart or table answering the question plus that README.

title_zh: Build morning routine and vacuum automations
summary_zh: A commenter had Claude help build a button-triggered morning routine for their daughter and a robot vacuum dispatch when the litter box cycles.
prompt_en: Help me create two Home Assistant automations. First, a morning routine for my [child] triggered by pressing [button or device] that does [lights, music, announcements, etc.]. Second, send my robot vacuum [model] to clean when [trigger, e.g. the litter box finishes a cycle]. Give me the YAML with my entity names as placeholders, explain how to find the right entities, and stop when I have both automations ready to paste in and test.

title_zh: Pull nutrition and fitness data into one dashboard
summary_zh: A poster set up a tracker via Claude in Chrome that gathers Cronometer and Fitbit or Google Health data in one place.
prompt_en: Using my logged-in browser, open [Cronometer] and [Fitbit or Google Health] and pull my [calories, macros, steps, sleep, weight] for the last [number] days. Put them in one table or simple dashboard in [Google Sheet or local HTML file], one row per day. Don't change any settings or data on those sites, and stop when the combined view is ready and you have told me any days with missing data.

title_zh: Find, enrich and push sales prospects into HubSpot
summary_zh: A commenter uses Claude connected to Clay and HubSpot to find organizations and contacts, enrich records, and push them into HubSpot.
prompt_en: Find [number] organizations matching this profile: [industry, size, region, other criteria], and the best contacts at each with the title [target job titles]. Enrich each record with [fields such as email, website, headcount, LinkedIn] using Clay. Before adding anything to HubSpot, show me the full list in a table and wait for my approval. You are done when the approved records are in HubSpot with no duplicates of existing contacts.

title_zh: Automate PR reviews and changelogs with GitHub Actions
summary_zh: Author runs Claude Code autonomously in GitHub Actions in production to review PRs, analyze test failures, generate changelogs and turn issue specs into implementation stubs.
prompt_en: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow in my repo [repo name] that runs Claude Code on every new pull request to review the diff and post a summary comment with any bugs or risks it finds. Also add a step that drafts a changelog entry from merged PRs under [changelog file path]. Show me the workflow file and wait for my approval before committing it or adding any secrets.

title_zh: Add unit tests to a forgotten Node.js backend
summary_zh: Claude Code read AGENTS.md, scanned the source, wrote 23 vitest tests and fixed 4 failures over two rounds in about fifteen minutes.
prompt_en: Read the project docs and source in [project folder], then add unit tests with [test framework, e.g. vitest] covering the main modules and routes. Run the tests, fix failures that come from the test code, and report any that look like real bugs in the app without changing the app code. Finish with a summary of what's covered and the pass count.

title_zh: Let an agent run a business autonomously from zero
summary_zh: Author set up Claude Code with memory and a decision log to pick moves each session; over 31 sessions across five markets it earned $0.
prompt_en: Act as an autonomous operator trying to make my first $[target] in [market or niche]. Keep a memory file and a decision log, and at the start of each session review them and choose one next move with your reasoning. Pause and show me before spending money, creating accounts, or publishing anything, and end each session by logging results and a recommended next step.

title_zh: Build and run an affiliate marketing site with sub-agents
summary_zh: Author used an agent with specialised sub-agents to build and operate a 729-page affiliate site, reporting $1,422 revenue in 30 days, reviewing public work and approving releases.
prompt_en: Build and run an affiliate site about [niche] using specialised sub-agents for research, writing, SEO and publishing. Draft the pages and a publishing plan, and show me each batch for approval before anything goes live or any affiliate account is signed up for. Each week, report pages published, traffic and revenue so I can review it.

title_zh: Have an autonomous agent try to earn its first dollar
summary_zh: An autonomous agent built products and a research reproduction but kept getting accounts banned, earning $0 after twelve days.
prompt_en: Try to earn a first dollar online in [area, e.g. digital products or freelance research] with a budget of $[amount]. Propose three concrete plans with the risks of each, including platform rules that could get an account banned, and wait for me to pick one. Pause before creating any account, spending money, or posting anything publicly.

title_zh: Run content marketing and TikTok posting with Claude
summary_zh: A commenter has Claude find social conversations, research SEO topics, write articles, generate short videos, and post TikToks every six hours hands-free.
prompt_en: I run marketing for [my business/product], which helps [target audience] with [problem]. Find 10 recent social conversations where people are asking about [topic], research 5 SEO topics that match, and draft one article for the best topic plus a 30-second TikTok script for it. Finish with a content plan table listing each piece, its channel, and a proposed posting time every [6] hours, and pause for my approval before anything is posted or published.

title_zh: Prepare bulk social posts for Buffer or Metricool
summary_zh: A commenter has Claude write captions and a CSV for bulk scheduling in Buffer or Metricool, since it can't post to Instagram or TikTok directly.
prompt_en: I'm promoting [brand or product] to [audience] on [Instagram/TikTok/both]. Write [20] social captions with hashtags in a [tone] voice, built around [themes or products], and put them in a CSV with columns for date, time, platform, caption, and media filename, spaced out over [number] weeks. It's finished when the CSV matches the bulk upload format for [Buffer/Metricool] and I've reviewed the captions before importing.

title_zh: QA your app and check failed deployments from your phone
summary_zh: A developer used Grok Bot to test their own app remotely and check failed deployments, and earlier to chase a A$17.49 refund via a website's live chat.
prompt_en: Please QA my app at [app URL] by logging in with the test account [test login] and walking through these flows: [sign up, checkout, key features]. Also check [hosting or CI service, e.g. Vercel or GitHub Actions] for failed deployments in [project name] and read the logs. When you finish, send me a short report listing each bug you found with steps to reproduce it, plus the likely cause of any failed deployment. Do not redeploy, change settings, or submit any real payment without showing me first and getting my approval.

title_zh: Handle LinkedIn backlog and life admin tasks with a bot
summary_zh: Mollie Mueller used Grok Bot to sort LinkedIn messages after maternity leave, restore her banner, email a vendor for a quote, renew parking permits and find toddler classes.
prompt_en: Help me clear my life admin backlog. Start with my LinkedIn messages: sort them into reply now, reply later and ignore, and draft replies for the first group. Then do these tasks: [email [vendor] to request a quote for [job], renew [parking permit or similar], find [kind of classes] near [my area] for a [age] child]. Finish with a summary of what is done and what still needs me. Before sending any email, submitting a form or making a payment, pause and show me exactly what you are about to do.

title_zh: Run personal assistant, content and brand-deal bots
summary_zh: The author built three Grok Bot agents: one as personal assistant, one repurposing newsletters and replying to YouTube comments, and one handling brand deals including an NDA.
prompt_en: Act as my assistant for [my work, e.g. newsletter and YouTube channel]. Each [day or week], take my latest [newsletter issue] and turn it into [format, e.g. 3 social posts and a short video script], and draft replies to new comments on [channel or platform] in my voice, which is [tone description]. Done means a single list of drafts for me to review, nothing posted. Before posting, replying, sending any message or signing anything, show me the exact text and wait for my approval.

title_zh: Order groceries from Walmart via a shopping agent
summary_zh: The author tried an agent to browse, add to cart and check out at Walmart; it took over 16 minutes and ultimately failed.
prompt_en: Go to [Walmart.com or my grocery store's site] while I'm logged in and add these items to my cart: [list of items with quantities and any brand or size preferences]. If an item is unavailable, suggest a close substitute instead of picking one yourself. Stop when the cart is complete and show me the items, prices, and total. Pause before checkout or payment and wait for my approval.

title_zh: Get a daily digest of top AI-agent posts from social feeds
summary_zh: The author asked Muse to send the 5 best AI-agent posts from their Threads and Instagram feeds each morning at 8; it created a scheduled task and sent a first, general report.
prompt_en: Every morning at [8am, my time zone], look through my [Threads and Instagram] feeds and pick the [5] best posts about [topic, e.g. AI agents]. Send me a short digest with a one-line summary of each post and a link, favoring posts with new ideas over general news. Set this up as a recurring scheduled task, run it once now so I can see the format, and ask me before changing anything on my accounts.

title_zh: Run content, scheduling, reminders and research with Muse
summary_zh: A team used Muse for several days on content management, scheduling, reminders, research and testing private MCP tools, noting odd interfaces, popups, logins and CAPTCHAs can still confuse it.
prompt_en: Act as my assistant for the next [few days]. Help me with [content planning, scheduling, reminders, and quick research on topics I give you]. For each task, tell me what you did and flag anything that got stuck on a login, popup, or CAPTCHA instead of guessing. Before sending any message, publishing anything, or changing my calendar, show me exactly what you're about to do and wait for my approval.

title_zh: Self-host open-source apps by having an agent do the setup
summary_zh: The author has an agent SSH into a local server and install self-hosted apps (e.g. baby tracking, finance tracking), then set up a Cloudflare tunnel.
prompt_en: SSH into my home server at [server address and username] and install [self-hosted app, e.g. a baby tracker or personal finance tracker] using Docker, keeping its data in a persistent folder. Then set up a Cloudflare tunnel so I can reach it at [my domain or subdomain], and confirm the app loads through that address. Before you open anything to the internet, change firewall rules, or delete any files, pause and show me exactly what you plan to do.

title_zh: Book an appointment using ChatGPT Agent mode
summary_zh: The agent checked Google Calendar for free time and sent an appointment email, but was about 10x slower than manual, the session expired, and the chosen time conflicted.
prompt_en: Check my Google Calendar for free time over the next [number] days, then find the booking page or email address for [provider, e.g. my dentist] and propose an appointment that fits [duration] and avoids my existing events. Double-check the chosen slot against my calendar for conflicts. Do not submit the booking form or send any email until you show me the exact time and message and I approve it.

title_zh: Automate repetitive web research into tables
summary_zh: The poster uses Claude Code with Browser Use and Chrome so a browser agent navigates, extracts and structures web data, returning results in a table.
prompt_en: Use a browser tool to visit [list of websites or search pages] and collect [data fields, e.g. product name, price, rating, link] for [topic or query]. Put the results in a table, save it as a CSV at [file path], and note any pages you could not read or values you were unsure about. Stop once you have covered [number] items or all listed sources, and show me the table.

title_zh: Build a competitor intelligence tool for evidence search
summary_zh: The author tested an agent on competitor research and built a tool to automate evidence search and assessment, noting mistakes in source weighting, deduplication and unsupported certainty.
prompt_en: Build me a small tool that researches [competitor name or list] on [question, e.g. pricing, features, recent launches] by searching [sources or search terms] and collecting evidence with source links. It should remove duplicate sources, weight sources by reliability (primary sources over blog posts and rumors), and label each claim as confirmed, likely, or unsupported rather than stating everything with certainty. Finish by running it on [one competitor] and showing me the report so I can check it.

title_zh: Answer Canadian statistics questions from official data sources
summary_zh: MapleStats connects an AI to 186 official Canadian data sources so it can return accurate figures like unemployment rates and rents; the author reports 8% to 92% accuracy on a 53-question benchmark.
prompt_en: I need accurate statistics about [topic, e.g. unemployment rate or average rent] for [Canadian region or city] and [time period]. Look only at official sources such as Statistics Canada or CMHC, and give me each figure with the table name, release date, and a link. If you cannot find an official number, say so instead of estimating, and stop once you have answered all of these questions: [list your questions].

title_zh: Scale ML innovations across ads ranking models with AI agents
summary_zh: Meta engineering describes using AI agents to help scale ML innovations across its ads ranking models; the post gives only the headline.
prompt_en: In my repository at [path or repo name], I have a model improvement that worked on [model A, e.g. a ranking model]: [short description of the change]. Find other models in the codebase with a similar structure, such as [model B, model C], and propose how to apply the same change to each one. Make the changes on a new branch, run the existing tests, and stop with a summary of which models changed and which results need my review. Pause and show me the plan before editing any files or pushing anything.

title_zh: Scan job listings and compile contact lists with Operator
summary_zh: Early Operator users had it scan job listings against a resume, compile details on 50 financial YouTubers with LinkedIn and emails, and test local dev environments; some sites blocked it.
prompt_en: Search [job sites] for [job title] roles in [location] and compare each listing against my resume at [resume location or pasted text]. Build a table of the 15 best matches with company, role, link, and why it fits. Stop when the table is done. Do not submit any applications or forms, and tell me if a site blocks you.

title_zh: Set up news alerts with a browser agent
summary_zh: Testers had Operator set up news alerts and save a summary; it followed a logical path but was slow and Google blocked login, so they leaned toward cancelling.
prompt_en: Set up news alerts for [topic or company] using [alert service, e.g. Google Alerts] with [frequency]. Then save a short summary of the alerts you created and their settings in [place to save]. Before submitting any sign-in or subscription form, pause and show me what you are about to do. If a login is blocked, stop and tell me.

title_zh: Work across Gmail and Google Drive in a shared chat
summary_zh: A user connected Muse to Google Drive and Gmail in a shared chat so it works across those services in ongoing conversations.
prompt_en: I have connected my Gmail and Google Drive. Find [the documents or emails I need, e.g. last quarter's invoices from vendor X] and put the key details into a short summary with links to each source. Stop when the summary is complete. Do not send, share, move, or delete anything without showing me first.

title_zh: Buy groceries through a Walmart+ account
summary_zh: A user gave Muse access to their Walmart+ account to buy groceries and tested it against manual shopping.
prompt_en: Using my Walmart+ account, build a grocery cart from this list: [items and quantities], with a budget of [amount] and delivery or pickup on [date]. Substitute only with [my rules on substitutions]. Stop at checkout and show me the full cart and total, and do not place the order until I approve.

title_zh: Update a website automatically
summary_zh: A user says Muse automatically updates their site on their behalf.
prompt_en: Update my website at [site address] with these changes: [list of updates, e.g. new hours, a new blog post]. Show me exactly what will change before you publish anything. After I approve, make the changes and send me a link to check each updated page.

title_zh: Clean up a Facebook timeline (ended in suspension)
summary_zh: A user had Muse clean up their Facebook timeline and believes this contributed to an account suspension.
prompt_en: Review my Facebook timeline and list old posts that match [criteria, e.g. before 2018, contain tagged photos of others] as candidates for removal. Do not delete or change anything. Show me the list and wait for my approval, and work in small batches at a normal human pace so I don't trigger account limits.

title_zh: Process GitHub issues into pull requests overnight
summary_zh: A cron job triggers an OpenClaw agent to pick one unstarted GitHub issue, implement and test the change, open a PR, and relabel the issue ai-completed.
prompt_en: Every night at [time, e.g. 1:00 AM], look at the open issues in my GitHub repo [owner/repo] and pick one that has no label and no one working on it. Implement the change on a new branch, run the tests, and open a pull request that links the issue. When the PR is open, relabel the issue [ai-completed] and stop, and do not merge anything or touch more than one issue per run.

title_zh: Run coding agents and experiments overnight while asleep
summary_zh: OpenClaw drove coding agents from 12:30AM to 7AM, and another user's overnight cron spawns experiment subagents whose results he reviews each morning as decision records.
prompt_en: Set up a nightly job at [time, e.g. 12:30 AM] that works on [project or repo] while I sleep. It should start coding agents on the top items from [my task list or backlog], and for any open question it should run a small experiment and write a short decision record covering what was tried, the result, and a recommendation. Have it all ready as a morning summary by [7 AM], and do not merge, deploy, or delete anything without my approval.

title_zh: Run slow background reports and research on a Mac mini
summary_zh: OpenClaw on a Mac mini handles sales reports, inventory checks, and roughly 30-minute research tasks in the background, alongside Cowork.
prompt_en: Handle these slow background jobs for me: [weekly sales report from source], [inventory check against threshold or supplier list], and research on [topic] that may take about 30 minutes. For each one, save the finished result as a short document in [folder] and message me when it is ready with the three most important findings. Do not send anything to other people or change any data in my systems without showing me first.

title_zh: List a broken iPad for sale with optimal pricing
summary_zh: A user had ChatGPT Agent create a listing for a cracked-screen iPad from two photos and shipping details, researching similar listings for price and starting bid; it sold for $60.
prompt_en: I want to sell my [item, e.g. iPad with a cracked screen] and I am attaching [number] photos plus these details: [condition, accessories, shipping location and method]. Research similar sold and active listings on [marketplace, e.g. eBay], then draft a complete listing with a title, honest description, suggested starting price or bid, and shipping settings. Show me the finished draft and pause before you publish anything.
